title: Implement a New 'PENDING_REVIEW' Trade Status Across Multiple Sessions
description: The TradeUtility OneBox system requires a new feature to handle trades that need manual compliance review. This task involves incrementally introducing a new 'PENDING_REVIEW' status for transactions. The work will be split across three distinct development sessions to simulate a real-world workflow where a developer might pause and resume work. The agent must retain context between sessions to complete the full implementation, touching data structures, business logic, and creating new function stubs.

project_spec.name: TradeUtility OneBox
project_spec.description:
TradeUtility OneBox is an "all-in-one" command-line utility written in C that helps small brokerage start-ups perform day-to-day operational tasks—such as payment capture, internal transaction routing, on-ledger settlement, and regulatory audit extraction—without having to spin up multiple services. Built as a single executable, the tool embeds a lightweight relational store (SQLite) and exposes a REPL-style CLI plus a minimal REST gateway (libmicrohttpd) for scripting and integrations. Internally, the codebase follows a consciously simple monolithic layout: one process, one deployable artifact, one shared memory space. Yet it cleanly separates concerns through a header-oriented Saga coordinator, CQRS-inspired read/write façades, and a pluggable audit-trail subsystem so that junior engineers can trace the full payment-to-settlement flow in a single debugging session. The project focuses on utility value—speedy batch uploads, on-demand reconciliation reports, encrypted export of trades—rather than high-frequency trading logic, making it ideal for training, demos, and small production desks.

Within the monolith, the Payment Saga walks through authorization, capture, FX conversion, and manual review in a linear state machine saved in the same SQLite database. Command handlers mutate aggregates (orders, payments, positions) while Query handlers read from pre-computed views, reflecting a CQRS pattern without additional services. Every mutating step appends a record to an immutable AUDIT_LOG table and, when configured, streams the log to an encrypted file using libsodium. Settlement batches can be triggered manually or via cron, producing ISO-20022-style files for downstream clearing houses. Because all subsystems—payment_processing, transaction_management, audit_logging, settlement, encryption—co-exist in one address space, deployment on bare-metal or inexpensive VPS is trivial, reinforcing the project’s utility character.
dependencies: libmicrohttpd (very small HTTP/REST gateway for automation hooks)
cJSON (lightweight JSON parsing/serialization for REST and CLI I/O)
uthash/utarray (header-only hash/array utilities for in-memory caching)
GNU Readline (optional, enhanced interactive CLI experience)
